- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above recent peak for 3–7 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.33) mid-period, model underreacts; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days to avoid mean reversion lag.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is neutral (0.00) or mixed; add 1–3% to forecast if sentiment remains flat for 3+ consecutive days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-period sentiment shifts; apply a “sentiment decay” rule: if sentiment drops after day 15, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for days 16–30.
- If sentiment is high at forecast start but drops mid-period, model tends to “freeze” forecast; adjust downward by 1–3% per day of sentiment decline.
